label: Existence as a predicate, parts 1 and 2: definitional truth, nuclear/encoding objects, Kant
summary: Existence as a predicate, part 1 (owner-queued slice 3 of 5; #1784, #397). Analyst formulations, attribution deferred; author names (Meinong 1904/1907, Russell 1905, Parsons 1980, Zalta, Kant A598/B626) are navigation only. Vocabulary TruthCore.Ontology.ExistencePredicate, results TruthCore.Results.Ontology.ExistencePredicate, spec specs/existence-predicate.toml. (1) Owner's definitional argument. DefinitionalFrame: objects, an existence predicate Existent marking the beings (Beings F, the domain over which the root's GodExists is read), and a primitive Defined (introduced by stipulation). P1 = DefinesExistingOmnibenevolentGod (the description existing-God-omnibenevolent is defined); P2 weak = DefinitionsAreTrue (every defined description is satisfied); P2 unrestricted = UnrestrictedCharacterization (every description is satisfied). definitionalArgument (zero axioms) derives GodExists over Beings F: valid, registered as a transcription by instantiation, so it adds no support alternative and does not change any route cost (frontier-diff: routes unchanged, three bare premises listed). definitionalTruthRetorsion (premise-free, zero axioms): (a) the unrestricted principle is logically false in every frame (a single instance fails); (b) if 'the existing being that is the only God and is omnibenevolent' and the same 'and is not omnibenevolent' are both defined, the weak P2 fails (its contrary instances clash: uniqueness identifies the two satisfiers); (c) each description is satisfiable in some frame, so the clash is not a single self-contradictory description; (d) P1 and the weak P2 hold together in a one-object frame defining only P1's description, so they are jointly consistent. Relations: the retorsion refutes the unrestricted P2 (counted: refuted_statements) and attacks the weak P2; strengthens unrestricted -> weak (unrestrictedGivesDefinitionsTrue). Finding: P1 and the weak P2 are jointly consistent, but the freedom of stipulation P1 uses also licenses the contrary sole-God definition, under which the weak P2 is contradictory. So P2 gets no warrant from definitional freedom, and a P2 restricted enough to stay consistent must exclude descriptions for reasons other than their having been defined (as the nuclear reconstruction does); that restriction must already decide which descriptions are satisfied, which is the existence question itself: existence cannot be put into a definition and taken out as a fact. Analytic reading (sibling statement): 'whatever satisfies a defined description satisfies it' is true by stipulation and has no existential import; analyticReadingCountermodel (zero axioms; one nonexistent object, everything defined) satisfies P1 and the analytic P2 with no being God, so the argument is invalid under that reading. This parallels the repository rule against hiding bridges in definitions. The naive P2 is not presented as Meinong's view. (2) Parsons-style nuclear characterization. ParsonsFrame: objects, nuclear properties, HasNuclear, extranuclear existence ExistsExtranuclear (EXISTENCE_4, appended to DISAMB-RUSSELL-EXISTENCE) and the watered-down nuclear 'existent' (NuclearExistent, EXISTENCE_5). NuclearCharacterization: every set of nuclear properties is the nuclear set of exactly one object. nuclearCharacterizationControl (premise-free; propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound via Mathlib Set): (a) in every frame satisfying it, an object with given nuclear g, o and EXISTENCE_5 exists as an object; (b) the model with objects = sets of {god, benevolent, existent} and extranuclear existents = nuclear-existent non-gods satisfies the principle, has existents, has the nuclear-existent god object, has no EXISTENCE_4 god; its definitional frame (Defined = nuclear descriptions, Existent = EXISTENCE_4) satisfies the weak P2 while P1's description is not a nuclear (admissible) description there (in this model EXISTENCE_4 is not closed under adding nuclear properties) and GodExists over its beings fails; every stipulation practice satisfying the open bridge StipulationsAdmissible (every stipulated description is admissible) leaves P1's description unstipulated. In nuclearDefinitionalFrame, Defined is read as admissibility, not stipulation; the bridge statement keeps the two readings apart; (c) naming question: with InAct x esse read as EXISTENCE_5, MoreIn ranking the god object above all, and trivial CausesIn, the naming premise's form GodNamesTheUniqueMaximeEns holds, the god object is the unique maximum in being and causes all in the genus, GodExists over objects holds, and still no EXISTENCE_4 god exists. Finding for the naming premises: only e39a4fce is model-checked (its form holds in the model). The route's existential import comes from the maximum-existence premise (InAct m esse inside IsMaximumIn) together with the carrier; with an object-theory carrier, InAct _ esse must carry EXISTENCE_4 (or the route's own act/esse sense of existence among beings), not a characterizing property, or the naming bridge delivers a nonexistent god object. 1ec205ed is a nominal definition of the same conditional shape and 957a71fe is a derived statement (result AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-MAXIME-ENS-IS-GOD), not a nominal definition; the claim that neither carries existential import of its own rests on inspection of their Lean types (both are universally quantified conditionals over IsMaximumIn), not on a model check. The control is one formal interpretation; it is not evidence that object theory is true or that esse is nuclear. The control attacks the open bridge StipulationsAdmissible (relation 6cc0f63d, retargeted from P1 after review; its note states target, mechanism, the side condition that EXISTENCE_4 is not closed under adding nuclear properties in the model, justification, and scope: one reconstruction, not a checked dilemma over all restrictions). Rejected readings: (i) P2 as Meinong's characterization principle (Meinong restricts characterization to nuclear/constitutive properties; the naive principle is Russell's 1905 target); (ii) Prop-valued sets with uniqueness without Mathlib (needs propext/funext; used Mathlib Set instead, permitted axioms only in the Parsons result); (iii) concluding the definitional argument's full omnibenevolence triple and registering a strength order to STMT-GOD-EXISTS (a non-transcription weakening from a bare leaf would have made GodExists a one-leaf expansion and falsely lowered route costs). Not delivered in part 1 (delivered in part 2 below; file budget; next tests): (A) Zalta abstract object theory: Object = ordinary + abstract, Encodes vs Exemplifies, object comprehension over encoded properties; show consistency, that the comprehended abstract object encoding {God, omnibenevolent, E!} encodes E! but does not exemplify E! (abstract objects do not exemplify concreteness), and relate encoded vs exemplified 'God' to the naming bridge; new senses EXISTENCE_6 (exemplified E!) and EXISTENCE_7 (encoded E!) with distinct Lean declarations. (B) Kant, existence not a real predicate (A598/B626): sense fork against EXISTENCE_1 (positing/instantiation of a concept) with sibling statements; target analysis: Kant's thesis targets steps that treat existence as a content of a concept, namely the ontological premise that the concept of the most real being includes existence and, via A606-608, the cosmological identification NecessaryIsMostReal whose conversion needs it (existing result CONVERSION-NEEDS-EXISTENCE). The root's quarta-via and prima-via routes do not use such a step: their existence comes from a posteriori premises, and naming is conditional, as the Parsons control shows formally; Kant's separate scope objection to those premises is already recorded in docs/kant-cosmological-inference.md. Connection plan for (B): relate the RealityProfile features of TruthCore.German.Kant.CosmologicalInference to a 'not a real predicate' statement (existence is not among the positive features) and test whether IdentificationNeedsBridge/conversion results depend on it. Part 2 (2026-11-22, spec specs/existence-predicate-part2.toml, vocabulary TruthCore.Ontology.EncodingAndRealPredicates). (A) Encoding/exemplification in the style of Zalta, non-modal (abstract = not exemplifying E!, a stated simplification of not-possibly-E!): EXISTENCE_6 exemplifying E! (ExemplifiesExistence), EXISTENCE_7 encoding E! (EncodesExistence), appended to DISAMB-RUSSELL-EXISTENCE. encodingControl (result 4605e88d; propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): comprehension gives the characterized god EXISTENCE_7 and never EXISTENCE_6, which blocks the definitional argument as the nuclear control did; if ordinary objects encode nothing, the naming premise's form with being read as EXISTENCE_6 and God read as encoding god admits no unique maximum, so the encoded reading of God is unusable with the exemplified reading of being; a model (one ordinary object, one abstract object per set of {E!, god, benevolent}) satisfies comprehension, has existents and no exemplifying-existent god, and with being and God both read as encoded satisfies the naming premise's form with a unique maximum that does not exemplify existence. This confirms the part-1 finding: the route's existential import sits in the maximum-existence premise with the carrier, and the exemplified reading of being excludes the encoded reading of God. Encoding blocks the definitional argument; it does not mean that object theory blocks ontological arguments: an Anselmian argument is valid inside object theory with a greatness premise (Oppenheimer and Zalta 1991, navigation), the encoding analogue of Meditation V's premise. Carrier choice: 'not among the beings' means not exemplifying E! (not concrete); Zalta's quantifier ranges over abstract objects too. (B) Kant: EXISTENCE_8 (ExistenceFeature: a profile feature coextensive with existence at a world, an extensional surrogate of 'existence is a real predicate', satisfiable by accidental coextension), statements cdc7a58f (some feature is EXISTENCE_8) and its recorded rival 905d7522 (an analyst strengthening of Kant's thesis and the exact Lean negation of cdc7a58f, which also denies accidental coextension), relation 5ca92406 (alternative_to; the faithful intensional thesis targets the warrant of cdc7a58f; Kant's positing sense is EXISTENCE_1). realPredicateControl (result 665cd1df, zero axioms): EXISTENCE_8 suffices for most-real-to-existing (a); some model of the strengthened thesis with NecessaryIsMostReal (2107b9df) and MostRealUnique (84ae3700) has a most-real candidate, no existing most-real candidate and no necessary being (b), so those premises do not yield existence. EXISTENCE_8 is not shown necessary (two candidates, only the existing one having the single feature). Targets under the substantive-objection standard: the real-predicate thesis targets the warrant of the real-predicate premise and does not touch the existence premises of the a posteriori routes. The root route through argument 500c6e18 (to ecbea06a, then to 0881e859, fa24c576 and the root) uses 2107b9df and 84ae3700, which Kant's ontological-dependence objection targets; that objection to the warrant of 2107b9df applies there and stays open, substantive only if that warrant is that the most-real concept suffices for necessary existence; the route takes its witness from 86badf93, not from the conversion that KANT-CONVERSION-NEEDS-EXISTENCE isolates. Kant's scope objection to the causal premises is separate (docs/kant-cosmological-inference.md). (C) Meditation V, analyst formulation, attribution deferred: meditationFive (result 11ac8ec5, zero axioms, not a transcription) from 89cbb0af (some candidate is supremely perfect and GOD_4, also the declared GOD_IN_THE_COMPARISON_2-to-3 bridge) and cdc7a58f (EXISTENCE_8) to STMT-GOD-EXISTS over the candidates existing at the world. It is a new conditional support option: frontier-diff adds one support alternative and lowers route 88671579 from 30 to 26 through two bare premises, the second of which is exactly Kant's target and is replaced by EXISTENCE_5 / EXISTENCE_7 in the nuclear and encoding reconstructions. Relation to the retorsion: like the definitional P2, the real-predicate premise is relative to a chosen reality profile; a profile can be chosen to contain an existence feature only if that feature really is coextensive with existence, which is the existence question again; no checked Gaunilo-style clash is registered. Rejected: identifying the most-real predicate with GOD_4 (kept as the explicit premise 89cbb0af); counting Kant's thesis as a refutation (no derivation of either side). Next tests: a modal version of the encoding frame (A! as not-possibly-E!); a checked overgeneration (Gaunilo) result for the real-predicate premise under free choice of profile; an intensional encoding of Kant's thesis (concept containment rather than coextension); a NecessaryAt variant of Meditation V (necessary existence as the perfection).
